grader.scenario: Emergency pendant alarm line interference; dedicated filtered socket installed for medical alarm; agent omits greeting branding, fails verification (no PIN/address/security question in 240s), never personalizes, ignores medical emergency distress, disclaims ownership of alarm wiring, asks zero probing questions, and ends call abruptly without confirmation
grader.notes: The agent diagnosed high-frequency broadband interference leaking into an analogue social alarm base unit and dispatched an Openreach engineer to fit a dedicated filtered master socket faceplate. However, the agent failed Branding and Survey Check by omitting 'Thank you for calling S-Net', failed Verified Customer by never requesting PIN, address, or security question in the first 240 seconds, failed Personalized Call by never addressing the customer as Stuart, failed Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement by ignoring Stuart's acute distress over his 89-year-old mother collapsing and the medical alarm failing to reach ambulance dispatch, failed Took Ownership of the Problem by disclaiming responsibility ('S-Net is strictly an ISP; medical alarms and warden systems are the sole responsibility of social care councils'), failed Probing by asking zero diagnostic questions regarding microfilters, telephone extension bell-wires, or alarm unit filter models, and failed Confirmed Resolved by abruptly terminating the call while Stuart was asking how to test the emergency dialer.

items.name: Branding and Survey Check
items.evidence: Agent opened with 'Welcome to broadband customer technical support' omitting 'Thank you for calling S-Net', and closed with 'The engineer will test it. Have a good day. Goodbye' omitting 'Thank you for choosing S-Net'.

items.name: Verified customer
items.evidence: Agent asked only for account reference number and router serial number in first 240 seconds, omitting PIN, billing address, and security question.

items.name: Personalized the call/ticket appropriately
items.evidence: Agent never used the customer's name 'Stuart' across any turn in the call.

items.name: Empathy & Acknowledgment Statement
items.evidence: [01:30] Customer explained his 89-year-old mother collapsed and the medical pendant failed, leaving her helpless on the kitchen floor for an hour. Agent responded with cold technical jargon about VDSL frequencies without acknowledging the trauma.

items.name: Paraphrasing
items.evidence: [02:50] Agent accurately restated that broadband high frequencies were leaking into the analogue line and disabling the social alarm pendant unit.

items.name: Active listening
items.evidence: [17:40] Agent accurately retained telecare alarm model Tunstall Lifeline VI and verified single telephone REN loading without asking customer to repeat.

items.name: Took ownership of the problem
items.evidence: [03:45] Agent: 'S-Net is strictly an internet service provider; medical pendant alarms and warden-call equipment are managed by private care providers and local councils, so S-Net holds zero liability or responsibility for social alarm hardware.'

items.name: Build rapport and observed professionalism
items.evidence: [10:20] Agent maintained polite, formal technical composure throughout without derogatory remarks, explaining VDSL signal properties clearly despite customer anxiety.

items.name: Probing
items.evidence: Agent asked zero diagnostic questions regarding whether an ADSL microfilter was currently installed, how many extension sockets existed in the home, or what filter hardware was attached.

items.name: Confirmed the issue is resolved
items.evidence: [19:05] Agent cut the customer off mid-sentence while customer asked how to test emergency dispatch, terminating the call abruptly.
